question: does his own four-orbit move score as an outlier on union coverage, on overlap, or on neither, against random four-subsets of the menu?
criterion: a new vertex v SERVES an atom a when |N(v) n N(a) n A| >= 4; a correction set C counts when EVERY member of C is served by some vertex of the added set
reading: overlap is DEGENERATE -- random four-subsets average zero and nothing can score below zero, so it discriminates nothing. Union is directionally right and too weak to pre-register: about one random four-subset in five beats his own recorded move. So both statistics die cheaply and the set-valued rung is HIS craft rather than ours.
caveat: the statistic is sparse -- the mean orbit serves about one of the small correction sets -- so these are small-number comparisons with a wide interval. Enough to kill overlap and to decline union; not enough to call union uninformative in principle.
may_not_feed_the_frozen_rule: computed from his labelled move; it is pre-registered for a SUCCESSOR rule and did not touch the running one, whose freeze predates it
